PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
SUSAN BURROW'S REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS TO THE PROPOSAL FOR DECISION

I appreciate and support the ALJ’s recommendations in their PFD in its entirety.  Oncor and PUC staff exceptions do not correct the wrong-doings in this procedure.  I agree that this project should be denied, for reasons outlined in the PFD regarding the Applicants’ failure to meet public meeting requirements, failure of the Applicants’ to use current tax role data for mailed notices, and the overall need of the project.  
1. Lack of Notice.
The Applicants argue that “The PFD's findings are inconsistent with the well-established common practice before the Commission”, and that “The well-established practice before the Commission confirms that CCN applicants routinely add and modify route links after the public meeting(s) and before filing the application without holding additional public meetings, including in proceedings involving large numbers of affected landowners.”.  Using the precedent as grounds for dismissing due process.  The Applicants refer to several dockets of the past where this occurred.  

Let’s take a quick look at their examples:



*Docket 59315 should not be considered, because the ALJs ruled that Oncor did not fully comply with 16 TAC §22.52(a)(4) after adding/modifying links without sending public-meeting notice to newly affected owners. The process took place alongside 59475, and therefore not typical of  historical practice.  It was wrong for this application to be approved.  
For Import Path 2, well over 400 miles of new routes were added after any public meetings were held 9 months or more earlier.  Import Path 2’s post-meeting expansion was vastly greater than in the cited examples, large enough to amount to a large-scale redesign that added entirely new routes impacting over 1400 additional landowners.  How can 1 to 22 miles of new route in the example dockets compare to that of docket 59475, which included well over 400 miles of new routes?  It’s possible and likely that the the small amounts of added route in the example dockets could have been adjustments made to accommodate landowner requests.  Over 1400 people impacted by the 400+ miles of new routes on docket 59475 were not allowed to receive any prior notice, consideration, or planning participation before the application was filed.  It appears to be a blatant failure to allow that particular group of people the ability to participate, or have an impact on any proposed route, which could have possibly altered the outcome.  The Applicant’s assumption that a second public meeting was not required in this docket, based on the example dockets of the past, is in my opinion, a lame excuse for not doing the one thing that would have been morally right.   

2.  Using Old Tax Data.
In addition to no public meeting participation for newly added landowners, intervenors throughout the process argued that the Applicants' witness began obtaining property-owner data in December of 2025, and that old tax data was used for the notices mailed on March 26, 2026.  Quite of few impacted landowners received no notice until after it was discovered during the hearing process, and possibly some not at all. 

3.  Prudent Avoidance (Lack Of).
It was discovered that Applicants, probably partly due to using old tax rolls, failed to identify recently constructed homes, homes under construction, and newly platted neighborhoods.  A school, a homeschool, and churches were not considered, and travel trailers and deer camps were counted as habitable structures.  

4. Unsubstantiated Need.
ALJs acknowledge that circumstances that have changed since the PBRP was
approved by the Commission in 2024. Loads that were the basis for the PBRP are noted as being less than originally projected.  The types of large load
demand in Texas has significantly changed since the PBRP was adopted. 
ERCOT adjusted its load-forecasting methodology that reduced non- oil and gas load, in particular officer-letter-confirmed load from transmission service providers. 
Senate Bill 6 was enacted to address the risk that large-load interconnection requests (75 MW at a single site) might not materialize, and It establishes a process for studying the impacts of requirements for companies needing the electricity to build their facilities next to the power source.

These changes have direct impact on load forecasts.  In addition, Intervenors note that the PBRP load forecast, where 55% of the non-oil and gas load was based on officer letters, 6% was unconfirmed, and 6% was data centers.  That load forecast has not been restudied using ERCOT's adjusted methodology for validating those loads.

It was also noted that Applicants never truly determined the amount of generation available in central Texas to serve Permian Basin, and therefore, Import Path 2’s “need” was never substantiated.

I plead with the commission to not approve this application, which has contained so many flaws - all at the expense of landowner intervenors.  Please adhere to the recommendations of the SOAH judges.  Don’t ignore the demands of over 40 State Representatives, Senators, the Attorney General, the Railroad Commission, and other policy makers. Please don’t ignore the pleas of, and turn your backs on, tens of thousands of Texans.  Don’t set a precedence for large monopoly corporations to bypass due process and ignore public input to projects that severely impact large numbers of citizens.  Please don’t permanently scar the well-known beauty of the Texas landscape for a project that doesn’t have a well-defined need.  Don’t burden Texans with the unwarranted rate increases that will result from this project.  The whole magnitude of bad circumstances surrounding this docket warrants the decision to deny it.  
5.  Prayer.  
I support the PFD's findings and conclusions supporting denial.  If, despite the blatant flaws with this docket, and despite the vast amount of public rebuttal, the Commission approves this application, then I don’t agree with the recommended Route 894.  I do this because it harms my family and neighbors.  In this case, I recommend Route 296, with reasonable adjustments to avoid or maximize distance from Florence Elementary School, together with all other relief to which he may be entitled.
Ultimately, I respectfully request that the Commission adopt the Proposal for Decision's primary recommendation and deny the Application.
